issue_context.title: JSON deserialization for positional record throws exception w/ Source Generator
issue_context.body:
### Description

Following the instructions here: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/try-the-new-system-text-json-source-generator/ I created a new project, installed the latest build for the System.Text.Json package:

1. `dotnet new console`
2. `dotnet add package System.Text.Json --version 6.0.0-rc.1.21372.4`

Code:
```cs
internal record Person(string FirstName, string LastName);

[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonKnownNamingPolicy.CamelCase)]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Person))]
internal partial class MyJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext
{
}

Person person = new(FirstName: "Jane", LastName: "Doe");
byte[] utf8Json = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(person, MyJsonContext.Default.Person);
person = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Person>(utf8Json); // works
person = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Person>(utf8Json, MyJsonContext.Default.Person); // fails
```

This works when using the reflection based deserialization.

But throws a NotSupportedException: "Deserialization of types without a parameterless constructor, a singular parameterized constructor, or a parameterized constructor annotated with 'JsonConstructorAttribute' is not supported." although the record only has a single parameterized constructor, AFAIK.

review_comments: FWIW I added `useDefaultCtorInAnnotatedStructs` to the reflection-based object converter factory to cater to F# struct records, it may not be applicable in sourcegen scenaria.
It's applicable in one case so far, `KeyValuePair<,>` deserialization. More so I'm just trying to share the implementation between source-gen & non source-gen as much as possible.
How do we do this for the reflection side?

I looked briefly through the reflection implementation but didn't find anything special-casing record types. Without this filtration here, we end up generating code for a `System.Assembly`-typed property that was implicitly generated (which causes problems in user code due to the property being deprecated).

For now the goal with these Roslyn-Reflection APIs is to get the serializer tests to all pass. At a time when we want to ship these helpers, we'd subject them to the full set of System.Reflection tests to ensure behavioral parity.
nit: needed? (here and elsewhere)
Yup, needed. Moved an extension helper to this namespace.
Combine this with the `BindingFlags.Public` loop above?
Same as https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/56354#discussion_r682797261.
Seems like `lonePublicCtor` can be deferred until the `if` below

I tried to refactor this method a bit (on top of this simple change to share the logic between src-gen and non src-gen), but kept hitting failing tests. I prefer to do this in an isolated PR if that's okay.
It seems like an error of some sort should be provided, at least if that's what we do for reflection cases. Can we use ReportDiagnostic?

Yup we can use `ReportDiagnostic` for this since constructor selection can only be influenced with design-time config. Right now we throw a runtime exception instead, just like the dynamic serializer.
A run-time exception sounds better since it is consistent with the dynamic serializer.
Nit: not a huge fan of exposing internal helper methods as extension methods.
This just moves the helper to a shared file with the source generator which also needs the functionality. Other shared helpers are written extension methods..
More reasons why it should be a `class`.
I presume this concern is no longer applicable. Should it be changed into a property?
Thanks, will update in new PR to avoid CI reset.
nit\future: if this list grows much, we may want a shared JsonConstancts.cs file.
This _is_ the shared file.
